outcomes.text: Understand short recordings about everyday needs, such as shopping transactions, directions and instructions.
Understand factual information and ideas from announcements, messages, news, interviews and dialogues about familiar topics.
Understand simple descriptions of events, opinions, feelings, hopes and ambitions.
Find main points, specific information and details in recordings about everyday subjects.
Recognise main ideas, themes, opinions, feelings and attitudes in predictable spoken texts.
Work out the meanings of occasional unfamiliar words and expressions from context.
Understand short, simple written texts.
Understand authentic texts about familiar topics and situations, including articles, emails, blogs and letters.
Understand simple written descriptions of events, opinions, feelings, hopes and ambitions.
Locate main points, specific information and details in predictable practical texts.
Identify main ideas, themes, opinions, feelings and attitudes in predictable written texts.
Infer the meanings of occasional unfamiliar words and expressions from context.
Deduce the meanings of unfamiliar words from context when reading about familiar topics.
Take part in brief social exchanges and communicate about familiar topics to meet simple needs.
Hold unprepared conversations about personal interests and everyday subjects.
Describe past experiences, hopes and ambitions, and briefly explain opinions and plans.
Communicate with reasonable accuracy using varied relevant structures, tenses and vocabulary.
Link short spoken elements into a connected sequence using simple connectors.
Use suitable strategies to keep conversations going.
Use pronunciation and intonation features to express meaning and attitude.
Complete forms with simple personal details.
Write simple factual information using everyday vocabulary and expressions.
Write linked phrases and sentences about personal life, immediate surroundings and everyday subjects.
Produce simple connected texts about familiar topics, including plans, preferences, family, education, work and travel.
Describe past events, experiences, opinions, hopes and ambitions, giving brief reasons for opinions and plans.
Communicate with reasonable accuracy using varied relevant structures, time frames and vocabulary.
Connect short written elements into a coherent sequence using simple linking words.
Use definite and indefinite articles accurately.
Use singular, plural, possessive, countable, uncountable, compound and derived nouns, including noun phrases.
Use comparative and superlative forms, possessives, demonstratives, quantities and adjectives describing qualities, nationalities, colours, sizes and shapes.
Use adverbs of time, place, manner, frequency, degree, direction, sequence, comparison and superlative meaning.
Use personal, possessive, reflexive, demonstrative, quantitative, indefinite, relative and impersonal pronouns.
Use regular and irregular verbs in appropriate persons, numbers, tenses and forms.
Form affirmative, negative and interrogative sentences, imperatives, infinitives, gerunds, passives, phrasal verbs and dependent-preposition constructions.
Use verb-object infinitive patterns, about-to constructions, causatives and modal passives.
Use modal verbs to express ability, possibility, requests, permission, offers, advice, obligation, prohibition, necessity and past habits.
Use zero, first and second conditional structures.
Report statements, commands and questions accurately.
Connect ideas using coordinating and subordinating conjunctions.
Use prepositions and prepositional phrases for place, time, direction, method and other relationships.
Use cardinal and ordinal numbers.
Express quantity using forms such as enough, too much, too many, half, a quarter and a few.
Express dates, clock times, including the 24-hour clock, and years.
Use and understand expressions for telling the time, days, months and seasons.
Understand and use expressions for sequence, dates, duration, frequency, timing, seasons, past and future periods.
Use expressions such as afterwards, before, during, finally, meanwhile, next, since, soon, still and suddenly.
Understand calendar and scheduling expressions including days, weeks, months, seasons, moments, turns and relative dates.
Understand and use common adjectives describing qualities, conditions, emotions, size, appearance, difficulty, temperature and usefulness.
Understand and use common expressions for place, degree, possibility, frequency, manner and emphasis.
Understand and use cardinal numbers up to a million, ordinal numbers, fractions and other numerical expressions.
Understand and use common verbs for everyday actions, communication, movement, relationships, feelings, activities and practical tasks.
Use expressions for sequence, frequency, dates, days, weeks, months, years, past and future time.
Tell the time and use vocabulary for parts and measurements of the day.
Recognise and use the seven days of the week.
Recognise and use the twelve months of the year.
Recognise and use the four seasons.
Use and understand vocabulary for colours.
Recognise and use common colour words, including light, dark and metallic shades.
Use and understand vocabulary related to sport and leisure activities.
Recognise vocabulary for sports equipment, venues, teams, competitions, scores, awards and supporters.
Discuss participating in sports, cycling, skating, skiing, surfing, swimming, riding, scoring and winning competitions or medals.
Use and understand vocabulary related to hobbies and ways of spending leisure time.
Talk about fishing, concerts, music festivals, theatre, listening to music and watching different kinds of programmes or films.
Talk about climbing, drawing, painting, singing, playing musical instruments and writing creative texts.
Use and understand vocabulary for continents, countries, nationalities and compass points.
Use and understand vocabulary for educational institutions, learning, classrooms, subjects and studying.
Understand and use vocabulary for a school break.
Understand and use vocabulary for a class or group of students.
Understand and use vocabulary for a classmate.
Understand and use vocabulary for an exam or test.
Understand and use vocabulary for an example.
Understand and use vocabulary for an exercise.
Understand and use vocabulary for homework.
Understand and use vocabulary for a lesson.
Understand and use vocabulary for a mark or grade.
Understand and use vocabulary for a project.
Understand and use vocabulary for a question.
Understand and use vocabulary for an educational result.
Understand and use vocabulary for a school report.
Understand and use vocabulary for a school term.
Understand and use vocabulary for a timetable.
Use language for responding to a question.
Use language for asking questions.
Use language for carrying out experiments.
Use language for explaining something.
Use language for not succeeding in an examination.
Use language for knowing information.
Use language for succeeding in an examination.
Use language for practising a skill or subject.
Use language for reading.
Use language for revising.
Use language for studying.
Use language for making notes.
Use language for understanding information.
Use language for writing.
Use and understand vocabulary related to jobs, careers and workplaces.
Understand and use vocabulary for a business.
Understand and use vocabulary for a company.
Understand and use vocabulary for an employee.
Understand and use vocabulary for an employer.
Understand and use vocabulary for a job.
Understand and use vocabulary for an office.
Understand and use vocabulary for a salary.
Understand and use vocabulary for work.
Use language for being without employment.
Use language for earning money.
Use language for looking for a job.
Use language for obtaining a job.
Use language for advancing to a higher position.
Use language for taking a holiday.
Use language for ending employment due to age.
Use common greetings, farewells, apologies, thanks, introductions, invitations and polite responses.
Express reactions such as annoyance, interest, pleasure, disappointment and sympathy.
Invite people, accept or refuse invitations, and suggest meeting or doing something together.
